motivation: So far every system passed 'reads content' (MS-156/157/159). An analysis paper needs a case where the controls expose a failure that accuracy hides. TEOChat (ICLR 2025, temporal EO-VLM) receives dates both as prompt text and as timestamps, so it can be tested for image use, date use, and pair use in one run.
model: teochat/TEOChat via .venv-teochat, loaded and prompted exactly as code/sentinel_qa_teochat.py (fp16, run_inference_single, timestamps=dates, max_new_tokens 64); code/e8t_teochat_protocol_v0.py
data: sentinel_qa_v0_1 Q1 tiles with a yes and a no item (primary: the 192 tiles of MS-156; all 203 secondary). Italy (x1_italy_items_v0) is a later, separately registered run.
arms: date_swap (item images, other item's dates in prompt and timestamps)
validity: parse failure > 10% in any arm, or real-arm agreement with sentinel_qa_v0_1/answers_teochat.jsonl < 0.95 -> invalid_run

primary_verdict.reads_images: d_swap (by image gold) >= 0.10 with tile-bootstrap CI lower > 0

secondary_verdicts.date_use: uses_dates if d under date_swap scored by the dates' gold >= 0.10 with CI lower > 0, else no_date_use_detected
secondary_verdicts.pair_use: compares_pair if P(yes|real pos) - P(yes|[post,post] pos) >= 0.10 with CI lower > 0; post_scar_cue if |diff| < 0.05; else unclear

what_counts_as_a_caught_failure: any of: follows_text; uses_dates with d_swap not significant; post_scar_cue; or blank P(yes) >= 0.25 — reported as such, not as a general claim about TEOChat
what_this_does_not_show: TEOChat on its own training distribution
compute: GPU1 if no other user's process; may share with our own jobs
